setlist.title: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Wharf Rat** (2 reviews): Jerry sings an excellent Wharf Rat; The Other One into Wharf Rat is very good for the era [4][5]
- **Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks)** (2 reviews): Pig-pen sounds especially strong, singing rarities such as The Rub and Caution; Caution highlights Pigpen's vocal improvisation, with more interesting vocals than wild jamming [4][5]
- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha stands out with riveting guitar riffs from Jerry [11]
- **Me and Bobby McGee** (1 review): Bobby McGee stands out with riveting guitar riffs from Jerry [11]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The first set closed with a great China Cat into Rider [6]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One through Uncle John's Band fits on one 80-minute CD, with the band pausing only once and two classic jams [8]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): An incredible Caution grows directly out of a forceful Not Fade Away [15]
- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (1 review): Band slides into Caution out of Goin' Down the Road, probably the only time they did so [5]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Rub**: rare: 12 archived performances [16]
- **Pump Song**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [16]

## The recordings

- **gd71-03-18.sbd.yerys.1663.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 153 min; rated 4.21/5 by 28 [1]. Said about its sound: Only a few opening notes of Casey Jones are clipped; vocals remain. Truckin' first verse is missing, with weaker sound; Recording has some hiss; Good mix and quality sound [8][10][14]
- **gd1971-03-18.sbd.130560.MrBill.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 137 min; rated 4.43/5 by 7 [2]. Said about its sound: Remaster has better dynamic range, presence and clarity; several tracks are incomplete, fading in or cut [2]
- **gd1971-03-18.132491.sbd.mathews.wise.flac16**: soundboard; 12 songs; 90 min [3]. Said about its sound: Recording has cuts, abrupt reel stops and starts, and occasional reel warbling [3]

## Around the show

- The Dead played two sets of about two hours each; some first-set songs are missing from the tape [6]
- Deadbase X lists Truckin', Drums, Other One, jam, Caution, Feedback; the taping compendium reportedly doesn't list this show [12]
- The full show reportedly does not circulate; the tape cuts in during Truckin' [15]
- Reviewer thinks this is the only Caution of 1971 [14]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd71-03-18.sbd.yerys.1663.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by M. Wienke and Ben Yerys; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Soundboard on 7-inch master reel, to cassette, to DAT, to CD, via Ben Yerys and M. Wienke [1]
- **gd1971-03-18.sbd.130560.MrBill.flac16**: transferred by Bill Guarneri; source: Recording Info: SBD > R > C > DAT > CD; Transfer Info: CD > WAV > Sound Forge 10 > TLH > FLAC [2]. Also: Remastered, retracked version of shnid 1663 by Bill Guarneri in July 2014, with dead air removed [2]
- **gd1971-03-18.132491.sbd.mathews.wise.flac16**: taped by Bob Mathews; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Set 2 Only; 7 Inch Half Track Reel Master @ 7.5 ips(Recorded By Bob Mathews)- Transferred By Dick Latvala(Master Reel Playback on a Technics 1506 Reel 2… [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1971-03-17 Grateful Dead Poster - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1971-03-17-grateful-dead-poster/) [18]
- Photo by a Flickr member (All rights reserved): [Grateful Dead - 3/18/71 Fox Theatre, St. Louis, MO | Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26759946003/) [19]
- Photo by uncredited: [the page](https://www.flickr.com/photos/104729480@N03/26759946003/) [20]
